questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a plant cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell wall is present.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell wall:-**

 
 
• It is a rigid structure that surrounds the cell membrane and provides support and protection to the cell.
 
• The central vacuole in plant cells is large and occupies most of the cell's volume, unlike the small vacuoles found in animal cells. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• These are present in plant cells, which are responsible for the process of photosynthesis.
 
• They contain chlorophyll, a pigment that absorbs sunlight and converts it into energy.
 
 
 
• **Plastids:-**
 
 
• These are a group of organelles found in plant cells that have diverse functions such as storage, pigmentation, and photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts are a type of plastid that contains chlorophyll.

questions.question: Goods which are of durable character which are used in the production process are called ________.

__
 
• - Capital goods are durable goods used in the production process, such as machinery, tools, and equipment.
 
• - These goods are not meant for immediate consumption but are rather used to produce other goods or services.
 
• - Capital goods are considered an investment in a company's productive capacity and are often depreciated over time.
 
• - Examples of capital goods include manufacturing equipment, vehicles used for transportation of goods, and computer systems used for data analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• - Veblen goods are luxury goods that are in demand because of their high price and exclusivity, such as designer clothing and luxury cars.
 
• - Consumption goods are goods that are used for immediate satisfaction of wants and needs, such as food and clothing.
 
• - Complementary goods are goods that are used together, such as bread and butter or smartphones and phone cases

Solution Statement:

The correct answer is option 1. Capital goods are durable goods used in the production process and are not meant for immediate consumption. They are considered an investment in a company's productive capacity and examples include manufacturing equipment, vehicles used for transportation of goods, and computer systems used for data analysis. Veblen goods are luxury goods, consumption goods are goods used for immediate satisfaction of wants and needs, and complementary goods are goods used together

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental duty stated under the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To defend the country.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **“To defend the country” is one of the fundamental duties under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was introduced by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• It is the moral obligation of every citizen to protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens to uphold national pride, contribute to the country’s security, and respect its institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To safeguard private property:** The safeguarding of private property is not explicitly mentioned as a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution. However, Article 300A of the Constitution provides that no person shall be deprived of their property except by authority of law.
 
• **To protect dignity:** While dignity is a core value enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution, it is not listed as a fundamental duty. The Constitution promotes dignity through fundamental rights, such as the right to equality (Article 14) and the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21).
 
• **To manage religious affairs:** The right to manage religious affairs is a fundamental right under Article 26 of the Constitution. It guarantees every religious denomination or group the freedom to manage their own religious matters. However, this is not a fundamental duty.

questions.question: Ritusamhara or The Six Seasons is a classic of Sanskrit literature, written by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalidasa.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa** is one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and dramatists in Indian history.
 
• **Ritusamhara** is one of his earliest works and is a poetic representation of the six Indian seasons: Vasanta (Spring), Grishma (Summer), Varsha (Monsoon), Sharad (Autumn), Hemanta (Pre-Winter), and Shishira (Winter).
 
• The poem describes the beauty of nature and human emotions associated with each season in a vivid and evocative manner.
 
• Kalidasa’s mastery of language and imagery is evident in Ritusamhara, which is often celebrated for its aesthetic and lyrical qualities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tulsidas:** Tulsidas was a 16th-century Indian poet-saint, philosopher, and one of the greatest exponents of the Ramayana. He is renowned for composing the **Ramcharitmanas**, a retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi, a dialect of Hindi. His work is considered one of the greatest literary achievements in Indian history.
 
• **Ravi Kirti:** Ravi Kirti was a court poet of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II. He composed inscriptions that glorified the king's achievements, including his victories over Harsha. However, Ravi Kirti is not associated with classical Sanskrit literature like Kalidasa.
 
• **Harisena:** Harisena was a court poet and minister of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta. He composed the famous **Allahabad Pillar Inscription**, which details the conquests and achievements of Samudragupta. While Harisena's work is significant for historical documentation, it is not a classical literary work like Ritusamhara.

questions.question: ENSO is the phenomenon related to pressure conditions. What is the full form of ENSO?
questions.solution:
Solution:

- ENSO stands for "El Nino Southern Oscillation".

- It is a natural phenomenon that occurs due to changes in atmospheric and oceanic conditions in the equatorial Pacific region.

- ENSO is characterized by two phases - El Nino and La Nina - which have different effects on weather patterns across the globe.

- During El Nino, the sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific become warmer than usual, leading to droughts in some regions and floods in others.

- In contrast, during La Nina, the sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific become cooler than usual, leading to increased rainfall in some regions and droughts in others.

questions.question: _______ unemployment refers to the lowest unemployment level a healthy economy can sustain without causing inflation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural unemployment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU).
 
• It is the level of unemployment below which inflation starts to rise due to increasing labor costs.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment is determined by structural factors such as changes in technology, demographics, and globalization, and is beyond the control of monetary policy.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment can vary over time and across countries due to differences in labor market institutions, regulations, and social norms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Structural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It refers to the mismatch between the skills and qualifications of workers and the requirements of available jobs. 
 
• It can occur due to changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer preferences.
 
 
 
• **Disguised unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to a situation where workers are employed but their contribution to production is negligible or redundant.
 
• It can occur in sectors with low productivity or in economies with a large informal sector.
 
 
 
• **Frictional unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to the temporary unemployment that occurs when workers are searching for better job opportunities or transitioning between jobs. 
 
• It can be reduced by improving labor market information and reducing search costs for job seekers.

• **Vulcanisation**:-

 
 
• The process mentioned in the question is called vulcanization, which involves the addition of sulfur to natural rubber to make it more durable and elastic.
 
• This process was discovered by Charles Goodyear in 1839 and revolutionized the rubber industry, making it possible to create a wide range of rubber products that were previously impossible to manufacture.

• **Saponification:-**

 
 
• It is a process in which fats or oils are hydrolyzed with an alkali to produce soap and glycerol.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation:-**
 
 
• It is a process in which sugars are converted into alcohol or organic acids by the action of microorganisms such as yeast or bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Carbonation:-**
 
 
• It is a process in which carbon dioxide is dissolved in a liquid to produce carbonated beverages such as soda or beer.
